Feluda.description: Prodosh C. Mitter, known as Feluda, is a private investigator and the protagonist of the stories.

Lalmohan Babu.description: Lalmohan Babu, also known as Jatayu, is a friend of Feluda and a thriller writer who often accompanies Feluda on his cases.

Subir Datta.description: A sales executive and visitor who seeks Feluda's help regarding a burglary at his house, Golok Lodge.

Nihar Datta.description: Nihar Datta is a biochemist who became blind after a laboratory accident in America and lives in Golok Lodge.

Koumudi.description: Servant of Nihar Datta, who sleeps outside his room to assist him at night.

Mr Dastur.description: Mr Dastur is a tenant in Subir Datta's house, described as quiet and withdrawn, who runs an electrical goods business and is linked to the theft and the investigation.

Uncle Sidhu.description: A close family friend with an encyclopedic memory, often consulted by Feluda for information.

Suprakash Choudhury.description: An Indian biochemist who was Nihar Datta's assistant during the laboratory accident.

Jayadrath.description: A character from the Mahabharat, husband of Duhshala.

Duryodhan.description: A principal antagonist in the Mahabharat, brother of Duhshala.

Duhshala.description: Sister of Duryodhan in the Mahabharat.

Jarasandh.description: King of Magadh in the Mahabharat.

Magadh.description: An ancient kingdom in India, referenced in the Mahabharat.

Dhrishtadyumna.description: Brother of Draupadi in the Mahabharat.

Draupadi.description: A key female character in the Mahabharat.

Arjun.description: A major hero of the Mahabharat, known for his archery skills.

Yudhisthir.description: Eldest of the Pandavas in the Mahabharat.

Anantavijay.description: Anantavijay and Devdatt are the names of Yudhisthir's and Arjun's conch shells, respectively, in the Mahabharat.

Twashtra.description: A mythical missile in the Mahabharat that causes confusion in enemy ranks.

Ramayan.description: An ancient Indian epic narrating the story of Lord Rama.

Mahabharat.description: One of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India.

Kaliprasanna Sinha.description: A Bengali writer known for his translation of the Mahabharat into Bengali.

Hijli.description: A place where Feluda previously solved a murder case.

Corbett & Norris.description: The company where Subir Datta works as a sales executive.

Dinesh Choudhury.description: A client of Feluda who lives on Camac Street.

University of Michigan.description: A university in the United States where Nihar Datta worked as a biochemist.

Ballygunj Park.description: A residential area in Calcutta where Subir Datta's house is located.

Bangladesh.description: A country in South Asia, formerly part of Bengal, referenced as the Datta family's ancestral home.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in India.

College Street.description: A famous street in Calcutta known for its bookshops and educational institutions.

Lindsay Street.description: A street in Calcutta where Mr Sukhwani's antiques shop is located.

Germany.description: A country in Europe where Subir Datta's elder son lives.

Dusseldorf.description: A city in Germany where Subir Datta's elder son works.

National Library.description: A major library in Calcutta, referenced as a source of information.

zamindars.description: Landowners, often hereditary, who held large estates and collected taxes in colonial India.

babu.description: A term of respect or endearment in Bengali and Hindi, often used for educated men.

Golok Bihari Datta.description: The grandfather of Subir and Nihar Datta, after whom Golok Lodge is named.

Topesh.description: Topesh, also referred to as Topshe, is Feluda’s cousin and the narrator of the story.

Golok Lodge.description: The name of the Datta family's residence, named after Golok Bihari Datta.

Belgium.description: A European country, referenced as the origin of the large mirror in the living room.

Charminar.description: A popular brand of Indian cigarettes.

America.description: Refers to the United States, where Suprakash Choudhury had been a student.

India.description: The country to which Nihar Datta returned with his research papers.

Nobel Prize.description: A prestigious international award, mentioned as a possible achievement for Nihar Datta's research.

kurta.description: A traditional long shirt worn in South Asia, typically by men.

pyjamas.description: Loose-fitting trousers, part of traditional South Asian attire, often worn with a kurta.

Namaskar.description: A respectful greeting in India, similar to 'hello' or 'greetings.'

Dada.description: A Bengali term meaning 'elder brother,' used as a respectful form of address.

Ranajit Banerjee.description: Ranajit Banerjee is Nihar Datta’s secretary, who has worked for him for four years.

Shankar Datta.description: Shankar Datta is Subir Datta’s younger son, described as troubled, suspected of theft, and involved in criminal activities.

Inspector Bakshi.description: A police inspector from Calcutta Police investigating the murder.

Dr Sarkar.description: A doctor who examines Mr Dastur’s body after the murder.

Bhagirath.description: A servant who finds the missing envelope with research papers.

Godrej.description: A well-known Indian brand, here referring to a steel safe.

Soneril.description: A brand of strong sleeping pills.

East Bengal.description: A famous football club based in Kolkata.

Thums-Up.description: A well-known Indian cola soft drink.

Bombay.description: The former name of Mumbai, a major city in India.

Argentina.description: A South American country, referenced in a letter found in Dastur’s room.

Dalhousie Square.description: A prominent area in central Kolkata.

The New Corinthian Lodge.description: A hotel in Kolkata where Shankar and his gang are seen.

G T Road.description: Grand Trunk Road, a major road in India.

Pandavas.description: The five heroic brothers in the Mahabharat.

veranda.description: A roofed platform along the outside of a house; common in Indian architecture.

hookahs.description: Traditional Indian water pipes used for smoking.

ittar.description: A type of natural perfume oil popular in South Asia.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment worn by men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

chowkidar.description: A watchman or security guard in India.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed for its stimulant effects.

paisa.description: A subunit of the Indian rupee.

ashtray.description: A receptacle for ash from cigarettes or cigars, commonly found in Indian homes.

Sellotape.description: A brand of transparent adhesive tape, commonly used in India.

collapsible gate.description: A type of folding metal gate, often used for security in Indian buildings.

Professor Bagchi.description: Ranajit Banerjee's former professor, who provides background information about Banerjee's academic excellence.

Sukhwani.description: Mr Sukhwani is a tenant in Subir Datta's house, owns an antiques shop in Lindsay Street, and is considered shady.

Department of Biochemistry, University o.description: The institution printed on the envelope, suggesting a connection to scientific research.

Madame Tussaud’s.description: A famous wax museum in London, used as a comparison for Ranajit Banerjee's expression.

Dasharath.description: A king from the Ramayan, whose story is used as an analogy in Feluda's explanation.

London.description: The capital of England, mentioned as the location of Madame Tussaud’s.

kerosene lamp.description: A lamp that burns kerosene as fuel, commonly used in India during power cuts.

foolscap.description: A size of paper commonly used in India for writing, larger than A4.

ch-4: Department of Biochemistry, University of Michigan, Michigan, USA
